title: fix(anthropic): bind cache carriers to replay policy
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Anthropic cache-carrier retention could be recomputed from a model ID after a provider plugin had already selected a different replay policy. A provider-owned transient carrier could therefore be cached, or a retained carrier could lose its cache boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The LLM session boundary now records the provider-resolved carrier-retention decision on the user message, media projection preserves that fact, and the Anthropic transport consumes it directly. This keeps policy ownership at the replay boundary instead of re-deriving it from model naming.

## User Impact

Provider plugins that customize Anthropic replay behavior now get cache markers consistent with their selected policy across tool loops, turns, and image hydration.

## Evidence

- The 2026.8.33 backport review reproduced the policy disagreement with the GitHub Copilot provider's model fixture.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/anthropic-cache-carrier-parity.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-boundary.test.ts` — 36/36 passed after rebasing onto current `main`.
  - cache-carrier parity: 6/6 in 3.57s
  - attempt-session boundary: 30/30 in 48.70s
- The boundary suite is retained because it exercises the canonical session lifecycle where provider replay policy becomes model-visible carrier state; a transport-only test would not prove that producer-to-consumer handoff.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <six touched paths>` — passed.
- Fresh P0-P2 autoreview — scoped clean.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36089688429) is currently blocked only by the two untouched `main` Madge cycles reproduced locally with `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`; no PR-owned failure is known.

Production delta is +21/-5 (net +16) across four source files: one closed retention fact at the LLM boundary, propagation through image hydration, and removal of transport-side model inference. Tests are +76/-5 (net +71) across two files.
